commands.review_summary:
Adds a Feishu reply-session-initialization-conflict notice plus a mocked regression test for a direct-message dispatch rejection.

PR surface: Source +32, Tests +33. Total +65 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: make Feishu inbound dispatch reject with the documented conflict error and inspect the subsequent `sendMessageFeishu` arguments. A live conflict is race-dependent, so the provided evidence does not establish a deterministic real-channel reproduction.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A narrow mechanical repair can preserve the Feishu handler’s established recipient and thread-routing contract while retaining the intended visible conflict notice.

target.title: fix(feishu): deliver visible notice on reply-session init conflict (#108320)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Feishu channel, when a reply-session initialization conflict occurs (the load-bearing error `reply session initialization conflicted for ...`, raised after the bounded CAS retry is exhausted), `handleFeishuMessage` only logged the error and **silently dropped the inbound message**. The user received no feedback at all — the message vanished.

This is a behavioral gap versus the Slack, Signal, and Discord channels, which all deliver a visible terminal notice to the user on this exact condition. #108320 reports the Feishu silent-drop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's `handleFeishuMessage` catch block (bot.ts:1895) previously fell through to the generic "failed to dispatch" error log with no user-facing message. The fix detects the reply-session init conflict (via a local `FEISHU_REPLY_SESSION_INIT_CONFLICT_MESSAGE_RE`, matching the per-channel convention where each channel defines its OWN local regex and does NOT import the shared `src/auto-reply` `ReplySessionInitConflictError`) and, on match, calls the real `sendMessageFeishu` to reply to the originating message with a clear notice:

> ⚠️ Couldn't process this message because the session stayed busy. Please try again in a moment.

The notice delivery is wrapped in its own try/catch so a send failure is logged but never re-drops the original message.

## User Impact

Feishu users who hit a transient reply-session init conflict now get a visible, actionable notice in their conversation instead of a silent drop. No behavior change for the success path or for other error types.

## Evidence

- Regression test added in `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` ("delivers a visible notice when reply-session init conflict exhausts its retry (#108320)"): forces the real `handleFeishuMessage` dispatch path to reject with the conflict error and asserts the notice is delivered to `chat:oc_dm`, replying to `msg-conflict`, with the "session stayed busy" text.
- Full `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` suite: **95 passed** on latest `origin/main` (83653833914).
- Fix rebased onto latest `origin/main`; diff is `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts` (+34) and `extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts` (+33).

### Not tested
The conflict is a race condition (CAS contention during session init) that cannot be deterministically forced in a live channel E2E. Proof is the unit regression test plus parity with the existing Slack/Signal/Discord implementations, which use the same detection-and-notice pattern.
